title: observability-weekly-2026-08-17
content:
Week of 2026-08-17 - Observability team weekly notes

Owners: Aisha Patel (owner), collaborators: Lena, Omar, Diego, Maya
Drive location: shared_drives/engineering/observability

Summary / Highlights:
- Tracing: finished rollout of the lightweight span sampling filter (OBS-412). We reduced trace ingestion by ~38% for low-value client requests while preserving full traces for high-latency/error paths. Initial validation shows no regression in root-cause coverage for recent incidents.
- Dashboards: launched revised latency & tail-percentile dashboard per-model in Redwood Console. New panels surface p95/p99 for cold vs warm KV cache hits.
- Cost telemetry: prototype for per-route token-cost attribution is live in staging. Early numbers suggest a 7–12% difference vs current billing proxy for batched requests - investigating discrepancy (see WIP below).

Metrics snapshot (week over week):
- Total trace events ingested: -36% (after sampling rollout)
- p50 inference latency (hosted API): 64ms -> 62ms (small improvement)
- p95 inference latency: 210ms -> 198ms (improved with routing tweaks)
- Observability platform egress cost (estimate): +4% (higher due to increased dashboard refresh rate in prod)

Incidents / Postmortems:
- 2026-08-15: Intermittent spike in trace processor CPU causing 2-minute partial backlog (no customer-facing impact). Root cause: a periodic metrics scrape + trace-aggregation job coinciding on same worker. Mitigation: moved scrape to staggered schedule and added CPU guard to aggregator. Follow-up: OBS-431 to add autoscaling boundary for aggregator.

Work in progress / priorities:
1) Tracing sampling refinement (owner: Lena) - follow up on OBS-412:
   - Validate that sampling doesn't drop topologically-important spans (DB calls that link request to downstream jobs). Add unit tests that simulate multi-service fanout.
   - Deliverable: sampling rule matrix + test results by 2026-08-24.
2) Dashboards revamp (owner: Omar) - post-launch tweaks:
   - Add KV-cache hit filter in query controls (ability to slice p99 by cache_hit=true).
   - Add note to dashboard about instrumentation changes (to explain drop in trace counts).
3) Cost telemetry (owner: Diego) - per-route token-cost prototype in staging:
   - Investigate discrepancy vs billing proxy. Likely causes: batching aggregation differences and rounding in quantized models.
   - Action: run side-by-side tracing of token counts at inference runtime vs billing table for 24h window (ticket: OBS-438).
4) Alerting improvements (owner: Maya) - focus on reducing alert fatigue:
   - Tune noisy alerts for trace processor GC pauses. Implement alert suppression if backlog clears within 3m.

Standup notes / daily logs:
- Mon 2026-08-17:
  - Lena: sampling rollout completed in canary, saw expected ingestion drop. Working on test coverage for span dependencies.
  - Omar: dashboards deployed to prod v2.0, one widget query hitting timeout on heavy traffic - increased query timeout and added cached summary table to speed it up.
  - Diego: ran initial cost attribution job in staging; found batching variance. Will instrument extra metrics in the runtime to capture batch sizes.
  - Maya: adjusted alert thresholds for trace processor, saw reduction in PagerDuty noise during afternoon spike tests.

- Tue 2026-08-18:
  - Lena: added fuzzy matcher to avoid dropping DB spans named like "db-query-*". Still seeing ~1% lost spans in synthetic tests.
  - Omar: added KV-cache filter to dashboard controls; UX feedback from Data Platform positive. Planning release notes.
  - Diego: identified that quantized model tokenization rounding occurs at the runtime aggregation layer; opened OBS-439 to correct rounding logic.
  - Maya: working on suppression logic unit tests.

Open questions / Risks:
- Sampling edge cases: could we inadvertently hide a root cause that spans multiple services? Need to confirm through chaos-simulated traces.
- Cost telemetry accuracy: if per-route token accounting differs materially from billing table, should we show both numbers in Console or reconcile to billing? Product input required.
- Dashboard query costs: new high-cardinality panels driving egress/query cost - need a policy for default refresh rates and caching.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Lena -> 2026-08-24: deliver sampling rule matrix + tests (OBS-412).
- Diego -> 2026-08-20: complete side-by-side token-count run and report (OBS-438).
- Omar -> 2026-08-19: add release note and patch for widget timeout.
- Maya -> 2026-08-21: land alert suppression and provide PD playbook update.

Notes to self / casual items (typical Drive-style rough notes):
- "notes to self: check whether aggregator can be container-optimized for lower memory footprint - maybe try compile-time flags"
- Draft Slack post prepared to explain trace count drop after sampling rollout; include links to dashboard and RFC.
- Reference: Confluence page for Latency SLOs: /display/OBS/Latency+SLOs  (update required after dashboard changes).

Recent linked artifacts / tickets referenced:
- OBS-412: trace sampling rollout (done - canary ok)
- OBS-431: aggregator autoscaling boundary (in_progress)
- OBS-438: token-count side-by-side job (in_progress)
- OBS-439: quantized runtime rounding fix (open)
- Confluence: /display/OBS/Latency+SLOs
- Slack: #eng-observability (thread: "sampling-rollout-2026-08-17")

Retro / feedback from team meeting:
- Good: faster p95 after routing improvements; less noisy alerts overall.
- Improve: better coordination with data-platform when rolling out dashboard schema changes (we caused two dashboard refresh storms last week). Plan: have a "dashboard-deploy" channel and a one-line schema migration note in Confluence.

Next week focus:
- Finish sampling tests and decide final retention thresholds.
- Reconcile staging cost telemetry to billing table and propose UI approach.
- Harden aggregator autoscaling and finalize runbook for trace backlog spills.

If you want a quick tour of the new dashboard, ping Omar or check the Console link in the Slack thread.

END OF WEEKLY
